one_liner: Studies how matter and energy behave, from particles to galaxies.
job_roles: Research Scientist (Physics) | Experimental Physicist | Theoretical Physicist | Optics & Photonics Scientist | Nuclear Scientist | Instrumentation Scientist
industrial_sectors: EXT-RND | EXT-EDU | EXT-DEFENCE | AASSC | ESSCI | PSSC
entrance_exams: CUET (B.Sc) | IIT JAM (M.Sc) | CSIR-UGC NET / JRF (PhD)
ai_reason: Literature search and routine computation are exposed. Deciding which experiment is worth running, and knowing when a result is an artefact rather than a discovery, is not.
role_spread: [Theoretical Physicist] higher: logical, existential, openness / lower: bodily, conscientiousness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Science stream with Physics and Maths -> degree: B.Sc Physics (3 years), or a 4-year UG under NEP -> post_graduate: M.Sc Physics (2 years) — skippable with a 4-year UG at 75 percent -> fellowship: Clear CSIR-UGC NET / JRF for a funded PhD place -> doctorate: PhD (4-5 years). This is the entry ticket to a research post.
nuances: [degree_dependency] 'undergrad' is the ceiling of this four-tier scale, but a B.Sc alone does NOT get you a research post — a PhD does. The scale reserves 'professional' for statutory licensing, which research is not. Read degree_dependency together with after_undergrad: masters_required. || [after_undergrad] A doctorate is required, but the MASTER'S can now be skipped. Under UGC/NEP rules a four-year undergraduate degree with 75 percent allows direct entry to NET and to a PhD without an M.Sc. That removes two years from the runway and is not widely known. || [economics] The long runway is FUNDED, not self-funded. CSIR-UGC JRF pays Rs 37,000 a month for two years, rising to Rs 42,000 as SRF — roughly 4.4 to 5.0 LPA through the PhD. But it is a stipend, not a salary: no PF, no gratuity, and it ends. That is why cost_of_entry is low despite nine years.

one_liner: Designs studies and works out what data actually proves.
job_roles: Statistician | Biostatistician | Demographer | Population Researcher | Survey Methodologist | Government Statistical Officer | Clinical Biostatistician
industrial_sectors: EXT-RND | EXT-GOVT | LSSSDC | BFSI | HSSC | IT-ITES
entrance_exams: CUET (B.Sc) | ISI Admission Test | IIT JAM (M.Sc) | Indian Statistical Service (UPSC)
ai_reason: Running a standard test is exposed; deciding which test is valid for this data, and whether the study design can support the claim at all, is exactly what models get wrong.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Maths compulsory -> degree: B.Sc Statistics, Maths, or B.Stat at ISI -> post_graduate: M.Sc / M.Stat Statistics — the standard hiring entry -> employment: ISI, government statistical services, pharma and insurance recruit at PG
nuances: [entrance_exams] The Indian Statistical Institute runs its own admission test, which is the most competitive and most valuable route into this profession. The Indian Statistical Service is a separate UPSC exam.
